clips.text: First, find the hip bone and the belly button. A third of the way along that line is McBurney's point. Mark five to eight centimeters along the skin lines.
One smooth stroke along your mark, through skin and fat only.
Under the fat is the external oblique aponeurosis. Open it along its fibers, never across them.
The internal oblique and transversus come next. Split them with two retractors. Pull, don't cut, so the muscle keeps its nerves.
Lift the peritoneum with forceps so the bowel falls away, then nick it.
Find the cecum, follow its taenia to the appendix, and lift it gently out into the wound.
The appendicular artery runs in the mesoappendix. Clamp twice, cut between, and tie both sides. No bleeding before you move on.
Find the true base where the taeniae meet. Crush it, tie within five millimeters of the cecum, and cut above your tie.
Suction the field dry and check the stump and the tied vessels.
